newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo begins VX-478 HIV drug Phase II trials.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo begins VX-478 HIV drug Phase II trials.

text.p: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc said Friday partner Glaxo Wellcome Plc has begun Phase II trials of HIV protease inhibitor 141W94/VX-478 in combination with other HIV protease inhibitors.
The 24-week study will involve about 48 HIV-positive adults, and is being conducted at three U.S. sites.
Results will not be known until early 1998, a Glaxo spokesman said.

The study will test VX-478 for use as a two-drug therapy, using two protease inhibitors, Vertex said. Most AIDS therapy is currently based on a three-drug cocktail, using a protease inhibitor and Glaxo's AZT and 3TC drugs.

VX-478 will be tested in different combinations, using Roche Holding Ltd protease inhibitor saquinavir, Merck and Co Inc protease inhibitor indinavir and Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc's nelfinavir, Vertex said.
VX-478 is also being tested in three-drug combinations.
Vertex shares gained 1-1/2 to 45-1/2 early Friday afternoon. Glaxo ADRs were off 1/4 at 30-1/4.
